summary: Apple's upcoming September event is expected to bring new device launches, which will likely lead to the discontinuation of over ten current products from its lineup.

As part of this refresh, reports suggest that Apple is expected to discontinue more than ten current devices. This move is standard practice to make way for newer models and streamline its offerings.

Rumors also point to potential launches of the AirPods 5 and details about the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro line. These new products will likely replace some of the discontinued items in Apple's portfolio.

headline_marked: MapQuest app surges to No. 1 [[after refusing to rename Lake Ontario]]
headline: MapQuest app surges to No. 1 after refusing to rename Lake Ontario
summary: The mapping app saw hundreds of thousands of new downloads after defying a Trump executive order to rename the Great Lake to 'Lake America'.
details: MapQuest's decision to keep 'Lake Ontario' on its maps, defying a Trump executive order to rename it 'Lake America', has led to a massive surge in app downloads. The app climbed to the No. 1 spot in the Navigation category and reached No. 4 overall on the U.S. App Store.

The company reported receiving "hundreds of thousands" of new downloads, with app usage increasing to 50 times its normal levels. Market intelligence from Sensor Tower confirms this, showing over 10x week-over-week download increases.
This move follows a similar stance MapQuest took last year when it retained the name 'Gulf of Mexico' despite a presidential order to change it to 'Gulf of America'.
In contrast, Google Maps has updated its U.S. version to show 'Lake America', while Apple Maps has yet to make a change and has not commented on its plans.
The executive order to rename Lake Ontario came amid trade disputes between the U.S. and Canada, with the U.S. imposing new tariffs on Canadian goods.
